data.content: {"story":{"as_a":"user with a personal to-do list","i_want":"to view my task list with a status and a priority indicator on each task","so_that":"I can see the state and urgency of my tasks at a glance on the to-do management page","business_description":"The to-do management page lets the user manage their personal task list. This story delivers the read-only task list view: it shows the user's tasks, each with a status indicator and a priority indicator, and shows loading, empty and error states. The list refreshes automatically when a task is changed. Creating, editing, deleting and changing status are handled by other stories.","business_value":"The user can see all their tasks and their state in one place, so they know what is open, in progress or completed and how urgent each task is.","acceptance_criteria":[{"given":"The user has at least one task in their personal task list","when":"The user opens the to-do management page","then":"The task list view shows each of the user's tasks, with a status indicator and a priority indicator on every row"},{"given":"A task has status Open, In Progress or Completed","when":"The task list view renders that task","then":"The status indicator shows the task's current status text and a visually distinct mark for each of the three values"},{"given":"A task has priority Low, Medium or High","when":"The task list view renders that task","then":"The priority indicator shows the task's priority text and a visually distinct mark for each of the three values"},{"given":"The task list request to the backend has not yet completed","when":"The task list view is displayed","then":"A loading state is shown and no task rows or empty-state text are shown"},{"given":"The user has no tasks","when":"The backend returns an empty task list","then":"The empty state is shown and no task rows are shown"},{"given":"The task list request to the backend fails with an error","when":"The task list view is displayed","then":"The error state is shown with a message, and the loading state is no longer shown"},{"given":"The task list is displayed and the user creates, updates, deletes or changes the status of a task","when":"The backend confirms the change succeeded","then":"The task list is reloaded from the backend and shows the changed task without a manual page refresh"},{"given":"The backend read endpoint for all tasks is called","when":"The request is received","then":"The backend returns only the tasks belonging to the requesting user"}],"edge_cases":["A task whose status or priority value is outside the allowed values cannot be produced by the data model, so the indicators need only handle Open, In Progress, Completed, Low, Medium and High (open question: the PRD does not state how the view should display a value outside these sets)","The list refresh happens only after the backend confirms a change; the view must not show the changed state before that confirmation","A read by ID request for a task that does not exist returns a task-not-found error, which this story exposes through the backend read endpoint but does not display in a dedicated screen (open question: the PRD does not say where a single-task view is shown)","The PRD does not state how many tasks the list shows per page or whether it paginates (open question)","The PRD does not state how the user is authenticated or how tasks are scoped to a user (open question)"],"dependencies":["US-create-task"],"definition_of_done":["Backend exposes a GET endpoint that as separate, distinguishable views","Status indicator and priority indicator render for every task row with all allowed values","Task list refetches from the backend after a create, update, delete or status change succeeds, and does not update the list optimistically","Automated tests cover the loading, empty, error and populated states of the task list view","Automated tests cover the GET all and GET by ID endpoints, including the not-found case","Open questions on pagination, authentication scope and single-task display are recorded in the story
